newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cuts jail term on pregnant British teen.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cuts jail term on pregnant British teen.

text.p: A Moroccan court on Thursday cut to two and a half years from five the jail terms imposed on two British women, one a pregnant teenage hairdresser, on drug charges.
Casablanca appeal court issued its verdict in the absence of Sally Louise Griffiths, 17, said by her lawyer to be pregnant, and barmaid Claire Louise Martin, 28.
A lawyer said on Thursday that under Moroccan law, the jailed teenager would in principle be able to keep her baby with her in prison for two years.
"That is the age at which Moroccan women normally stop breastfeeding," she said. After that, a child would normally be handed over to relatives.
The court decision, read out in a brief statement without giving reasons, appeared to take account of this timing. Griffiths' sentence would end around the time her baby would be aged two.
Both women come from Harwich, southeast England, and were sentenced to five years imprisonment in August. The court maintained a 5,000 dirhams ($581) fine on each.
Their lawyer would not comment on the court's decision.
A British embassy spokesman said: "We have formally asked the Moroccan authorities what facilities (for care of the baby and mother) will be provided, to ensure they will be adequate."
Arrested on July 30 at Casablanca airport preparing to board a flight to Amsterdam, the two were each sentenced last August for possessing and trading five kg (11 lbs) of cannabis resin.

The defence, which had sought acquittals at the trial, said at the earlier appeal hearing last week that Griffiths was pregnant, was still an adolescent, had no previous convictions and should benefit from extenuating circumstances.
Police said the two women were promised 1,500 pounds ($2,325) by a British drug dealer in Amsterdam to carry the cannabis from a contact in Fez to the Dutch city.
Nearly 40 Britons are held, with scores of French, Spanish and other foreigners, in Moroccan jails for drug trafficking.
On Wednesday, an appeal court in the northern city of Tangier put off for a week giving its verdict in an appeal by David Richards, 37, from Alnwick, Northumberland.
Richards, who conducted his own defence after his lawyer withdrew, told the court he knew nothing about 222 kg (489 lbs) of cannabis resin found in his vehicle.

He was arrested with his wife Jill, 40, last August while embarking from Tangier for Spain with their eight-year-old daughter Victoria. He was jailed for five years, fined and his vehicle confiscated.
Jill Richards, who pleaded not guilty, was acquitted.

Two more Britons, Mark Leslie Darrington, 28, and his companion, Christine Sherman, said to be in her 40s, are awaiting trial on drugs charges and have been accused by Moroccan police of being part of an international drug network run from Spain.
Morocco has launched a crackdown on drug smuggling, notably in the north of the country.
